s2.ptxt: Using a plastic-faced hammer, tap in the straight pins at the positions shown in the illustration.
Using E8 and E10 torx socket wrenches, install the stud bolts at the positions shown in the illustration.
Using a socket hexagon wrench (5mm), install the 3 oil nozzles No.1.
Using a small screwdriver, install a new piston pin hole snap ring on one side only.

atten3.ptxt: Install the snap ring so that its end gap is within the range marked * in the illustration.

s2.ptxt: Heat the piston to approximately 80°C.

atten2.ptxt: The piston is hot, so always wear gloves when working.

s2.ptxt: Apply engine oil to the piston pin and the connecting rod small end.
Align the front mark of the piston with the front mark of the connecting rod, and push in the piston pin with your thumb until it contacts the snap ring.

atten3.ptxt: Do not change the combination of the piston and piston pin.

s2.ptxt: Using a small screwdriver, install a new piston pin hole snap ring.

atten3.ptxt: Install the snap ring so that its end gap is within the range marked * in the illustration.

s2.ptxt: Install the oil ring expander and 2 oil ring side rails by hand.
Using a piston ring expander, install compression ring No.1 and compression ring No.2.
Position the piston ring end gaps as shown in the illustration.
Clean the main journals and the inner and outer surfaces of the bearings.
Install Upper Bearing

s3.ptxt: Install the upper bearing to the cylinder block so that it is near the center.

item.ptxt: The bearings for journals No.1 and 4 differ in size from those for journals No.2 and 3; check them when assembling.
Do not apply engine oil to the bearing installation surface of the cylinder block or the back of the bearing.
The line of the cylinder block oil groove must be visible through the upper bearing oil hole.

s2.ptxt: Install Lower Bearing

s3.ptxt: Install the lower bearing to the bearing cap so that it is near the center.
Using a vernier caliper, measure the distance between the bearing cap edge and the lower bearing edge.

item.ptxt: Check the journal numbers on the bearing caps.
The bearings for journals No.1 and 4 differ in size from those for journals No.2 and 3; check them when assembling.
Do not apply engine oil to the bearing installation surface of the bearing cap or the back of the bearing.

s2.ptxt: Apply engine oil to the surfaces of the thrust washer set.
Install the thrust washer set to the front and rear sides of journal No.2 on the cylinder block with the oil grooves facing outward.

atten3.ptxt: Be careful not to install the thrust washer set incorrectly.

s2.ptxt: Apply engine oil to the upper bearing surfaces and install the crankshaft.
Apply engine oil to the lower bearing surfaces.
Check the protrusions and journal numbers of the bearing caps and temporarily place the caps on the block.

item.ptxt: Check the protrusions and journal numbers of the bearing caps.
Install the bearing caps with the protrusions facing in the direction shown in the illustration.

s2.ptxt: Apply engine oil to the threads and under the heads of the bolts.

atten3.ptxt: Tighten the crankshaft bearing cap bolts using the plastic region tightening method.

s2.ptxt: Push in the bearing cap until the clearance (A) between the cylinder block and bearing cap is 6mm or less, and temporarily tighten the 8 bolts at the positions shown in the illustration.

atten3.ptxt: The bearing cap bolts differ in length; check them when assembling.

s2.ptxt: Using a plastic-faced hammer, lightly tap the bearing cap to ensure it is fully seated.
Apply engine oil to the threads and under the heads of the bolts and temporarily tighten the 8 bolts.

atten3.ptxt: The bearing cap bolts differ in length; check them when assembling.

s2.ptxt: Using a socket wrench (14mm), temporarily tighten the bolts in 2-3 passes in the sequence shown in the illustration, then tighten them to the specified torque.

atten3.ptxt: Tighten the bolts while checking that the crankshaft turns smoothly.

s2.ptxt: Mark the front of the bolt heads with paint.
Using the paint marks as a guide, tighten each bolt an additional 90° in the tightening order.
Check that all paint marks have been turned 90° in the tightening direction.

atten3.ptxt: Tighten the bolts while checking that the crankshaft turns smoothly.

s2.ptxt: Install new seal washers, temporarily tighten the bolts in 2-3 passes in the sequence shown in the illustration, then tighten the 8 bolts to the specified torque.

item.ptxt: Tighten the bolts while checking that the crankshaft turns smoothly.
The bolts differ in length; check them when assembling.

s2.ptxt: Install the connecting rod bearings to the connecting rods and bearing caps.
Using a vernier caliper, measure the distance between the connecting rod edge and the upper bearing edge.

item.ptxt: Do not apply engine oil to the bearing installation surfaces of the connecting rods and caps or the back of the bearings.
Measure and position the bearing so that it is centered in the bearing cap.

s2.ptxt: Using a vernier caliper, measure the distance between the bearing cap edge and the lower bearing edge.

item.ptxt: Do not apply engine oil to the bearing installation surfaces of the connecting rods and caps or the back of the bearings.
Measure and position the bearing so that it is centered in the bearing cap.

atten3.ptxt: Tighten the connecting rod bolts using the plastic region tightening method.

s2.ptxt: Apply engine oil to the cylinder walls, the piston circumference and the connecting rod bearing surfaces.
Check the positions of the piston ring end gaps again.
Check the front mark and, using a piston ring compressor, install the piston with connecting rod.
Check the matching of the connecting rod and cap and the front mark of the cap, and install the cap to the connecting rod.

atten3.ptxt: Keep the connecting rods and caps in the same combinations as before disassembly.

s2.ptxt: Apply a light coat of engine oil to the threads and seats of the bolts.
Using a socket wrench (12mm 12 square), temporarily tighten the bolts in 2-3 passes, then tighten them to the specified torque.
Mark the front of the bolt heads with paint.
Using the paint marks as a guide, tighten each bolt an additional 90°.
Check that the crankshaft turns smoothly.
